table_description: UDTF returning a single-row snapshot of system-wide vital signs. CPU utilization, main storage pool sizes, ASP usage, address-ID consumption, and job/thread counts at the moment of the call. The first stop for 'how is the system doing right now?'.

table_columns.name: ELAPSED_CPU_USED
table_columns.description: Percent CPU consumed during the elapsed interval. Requires a prior RESET_STATISTICS call — otherwise reflects since IPL. For a useful instantaneous reading, call RESET_STATISTICS, sleep a few seconds, then read.

table_columns.name: CONFIGURED_CPUS
table_columns.description: Number of CPU cores configured on the partition. Pair with CPU percentage to convert to cores-equivalent.

table_columns.name: CURRENT_CPU_CAPACITY
table_columns.description: Active CPU capacity in physical cores. May be less than CONFIGURED_CPUS when PowerVM dispatches fewer.

table_columns.name: SYSTEM_ASP_USED
table_columns.description: System ASP (ASP 1) percent used. Above 90 is dangerous; the system pages aggressively. Above 95 risks IPL.

table_columns.name: TOTAL_AUXILIARY_STORAGE
table_columns.description: Total auxiliary storage across all ASPs in megabytes.

table_columns.name: ACTIVE_JOBS_IN_SYSTEM
table_columns.description: Count of active jobs at the snapshot moment. Sanity-check against ACTIVE_JOB_INFO row count.

table_columns.name: MAXIMUM_JOBS_IN_SYSTEM
table_columns.description: Configured maximum from system value QMAXJOB. Hitting this prevents new jobs from starting.

data_quality_notes: ELAPSED_CPU_USED is meaningful only after RESET_STATISTICS is called for the session — otherwise it reports IPL-to-now.
The UDTF accepts an optional argument to control whether to reset stats: TABLE(QSYS2.SYSTEM_STATUS_INFO(RESET_STATISTICS => 'YES')).
